boundaries.lookingBack: explains how benzo[a]pyrene activates AhR and induces CYP1A1 to form reactive epoxides that damage DNA

topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causes, mechanisms, and testing methodologies.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetic Basis, Bad Luck, and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and explore the interplay between intrinsic random mutations and environmental risk factors through public perception and global epidemiological studies.

topics.label: Biological and Molecular Mechanisms of Carcinogens and Tumor Promoters
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the specific cellular, biochemical, and developmental mechanisms by which infectious agents, chemical mutagens, and non-mutagenic promoters induce and facilitate malignancy.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing, epidemiological, in vivo animal, and in vitro assay methods used to detect, test, and prove that environmental agents are carcinogenic.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarizing environmental cancer risks and framing everyday exposure decisions as a balance of risks and benefits.
